evidence: Read complete Arabic, Turkish, English and all supplied Quran context (1:1–3). These are direct grammatical explanations of every component of canonical 1:1 «بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ». The repeated divine epithets also occur at 1:3, but here belong to the basmala discussion; no independent 1:3 mapping is warranted. TR begins «(اسم): zâid bâ ile mecrûrdur», preserves the intervening grammatical and poetic material, and ends with case alternatives for «الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ». EN likewise begins with اسم governed by bāʾ and ends with the same epithets and case alternatives. Both translations follow this source entry throughout. evidence: Read complete Arabic, Turkish, English and Quran context 1:3–7. The opening «إِيَّاكَ نصب بوقوع نَعْبُدُ عليه» explains the object and pronominal construction in the first clause of 1:5. «نَعْبُدُ فعل مستقبل» analyzes its verb; «وإِيَّاكَ منصوب بنستعين عطف جملة على جملة» explicitly moves to the second clause, followed by the dialectal reading and derivation of نستعين and استعانة through the closing «ولزمت الهاء عوضا». All anchors belong to canonical 1:5 «إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ». Generic grammatical explanations serve those words and supply no other substantive verse target. TR retains the object discussion, imperfect-verb analysis and final derivation; EN does the same from the first accusative إيّاك through compensatory hāʾ. Both translations therefore follow this exact Arabic entry. The full cited live digital author passage at https://tafsir.app/iraab-alnahas/1/5 confirms these anchors and the verse assignment.

evidence: Read full Arabic, Turkish, English and supplied Quran context 1:4–7; additionally retrieved the complete canonical 7:156 with all available meanings to check the misleading opening. The Arabic literally starts «إِنَّا هُدْنا», a phrase occurring inside 7:156, but its entire explanation is «دعاء وطلب», deletion of the final yāʾ, a connecting alif, derivation «من يهدي», «النون والألف مفعول أول», «والصِّراطَ مفعول ثان», and finally «الْمُسْتَقِيمَ نعت للصراط». Those grammatical facts describe the imperative اهدنا and the two objects in 1:6 «ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ», not the declarative إنا هدنا إليك of 7:156. The opening is therefore source textual corruption, not evidence for remapping or adding 7:156. Live https://tafsir.app/iraab-alnahas/1/6 reproduces the same erroneous words but labels the passage with 1:6 and confirms every subsequent anchor. TR opens with اهدنا and translates the complete explanatory passage; EN preserves إنا هدنا, explicitly notes that اهدنا is the discussed word, and likewise preserves all the analysis. Both follow this source entry and its intended 1:6 mapping.
